notes.content:
[h2]Hey Car Dealers![/h2]

[h3]What’s new?[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]New junkyard station - car crusher[/b]
Prepare a car that’s 100% mechanically functional. It must be also rust-free, washed, and polished. Once it meets all requirements, you can crush it into a trophy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/7101297d74e995519199455b2e4ac4fccaecf3e6.gif[/img]

[*] [b]Trophies with multiple tiers[/b]
Trophies are divided into: common, silver, gold, and diamond. Each higher tier requires crafting a certain number of figurines. You can find the details at the crusher.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/1f0631fce89d6e280a29264bc742acb53101c50a.gif[/img]

Show off your crafted trophies in the office and impress your clients with your collection. Shelves are available in level 3 and 4 offices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/bb6f17b9db95bf55c6345883bdfe580df4a3df86.gif[/img]

A full vehicle encyclopedia has been added – you’ll find descriptions of every car, fun facts, and the new statistics feature. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/5aa9e04852d0a916bd141a9a4779c3282e5cf4af.png[/img]

notes.title: Repair System - Fuse Replacement
notes.content:
[h2]Hey Car Dealers![/h2]

[h3]Only 3 days left until the release![/h3]

In today’s devlog, we’ve got another batch of info about the [b]mechanical repair system[/b]. This time, we’re focusing on [b]fuse replacement[/b].

On the scanner report, you’ll notice a section labeled "Fuses." If the percentage shown is lower than 100%, it means that [b]some fuses are either blown or missing[/b].

Once you enter [b]Repair Mode[/b] and click on the [b]fuse box[/b], you’ll see their condition - blown fuses or empty slots. Thanks to the [b]highlight system[/b], you’ll know exactly [b]which fuse should go where[/b].

Here’s how it works:

- To [b]remove [/b]a fuse, just click on it.
- To [b]insert a new one[/b], click on the appropriate fuse on the right side, then confirm where you want to place it.

notes.title: Employees at Workstations How Do They Work and What Can They Do?
notes.content:
[h2]Hey Car Dealers![/h2]

Only [b]16 days[/b] left until the release!

In today’s devlog, we’re continuing our series about [b]room upgrades[/b]. One of the final upgrade levels for the workshop, car wash, and body shop introduces a big feature: [b]the ability to hire an employee[/b]. The hiring process is handled through an app on your in-game computer – just open it and choose the person you want to hire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/dbe3ba82fca03cef40c4e0e79a99a90435fa0337.gif[/img]

Once hired, the employee must be assigned to a workstation.
[b]Important![/b] - each employee has an [b]hourly wage[/b], and you’ll be [b]charged for each hour they’re assigned to a workstation[/b]. [b]The payment is settled once per day[/b] - as a single daily wage visible at the end of the day. Employees are not locked into specific roles, so you can freely reassign them between workstations as needed.

So how do you make an employee do some work?
It’s simple - just park a car in the area next to the employee’s workstation and [b]interact with them[/b].

In the [b]car wash[/b] and [b]body shop[/b], things are straightforward - the employee will automatically perform all the necessary tasks.
In the [b]workshop[/b], however, you’ll need to specify exactly what you want done. A dialog window will show all the parts installed in the car - you can instruct the employee to remove them to your warehouse or replace them with another part from your inventory.

Once confirmed, the employee will begin their work sequence, and a [b]progress bar above[/b] their head will show you how long the task will take.

We’re excited to introduce the day and night cycle, which not only brings visual changes but also makes the city feel more realistic. Managing time and planning your day effectively will be crucial, and every day in the game will have its own unique atmosphere.

notes.content:

notes.title: A New Way to Save Your Progress!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Car Dealers![/h2]

In today’s devlog, we’re going image-free, but we want to share some insights about our current work on the game. One of the key elements we’re currently reworking is the save system.

In the prologue, the gameplay was rather linear, so the save system mainly relied on checkpoints. However, in the demo, we are gradually opening up the game world to provide you with complete freedom in making decisions - what cars you buy, what you do with them, and how you manage your business.

As a result, we are rebuilding the save system to better suit the new gameplay structure. In addition to the option for manual saves, we are introducing an autosave system that will trigger every 2 minutes. Three slots in the save table will be reserved specifically for autosave, so you can easily revert to one of the earlier game states if needed.

This is just one of many changes we plan to make to enhance your experience in Car Dealer Simulator and make it even more immersive and satisfying. Thank you for your continued support, and we look forward to hearing your feedback!

[h2]Hello everyone! 👋[/h2]

In today’s devlog, we’re excited to introduce the interactive map and GPS system that will make managing tasks and navigating the city much more convenient. Both key Points of Interest (POIs) and available tasks are now displayed on the map, making it quick and intuitive to plan your next moves.

The map in our game serves as the central hub for managing your activities around the city. Here’s what you’ll find:

[list]
[*]Points of Interest (POIs) – key locations such as:
[list]
[*]Gas Station – for refueling your vehicles.
[*]Parts Shop – to stock up on tools and parts.
[*]Workshop – your everyday workspace.
[/list]
[*]Tasks – icons representing missions you can take on, such as picking up a car from a client or delivering a vehicle to a specific location.
[/list]
Clicking on any marker – whether it’s a POI or a task – will automatically set a route in the GPS, helping you reach your destination with ease.

[*]Map filtering
If you want to see only a specific type of marker, such as tasks or certain POIs, you can enable the appropriate filter. This is perfect for planning when you have multiple errands to run.
[*]Dynamic route planning
Clicking on a marker automatically plots the shortest route to your destination. The GPS will guide you from your current location, showing the route on the map and the in-game HUD.

notes.title: Get Fueled Up – Refueling Mechanics in Car Dealer Simulator
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/b038bb3c286d5f9f026e828d3001f906a7136f60.png[/img]

[h2]Hey, car dealers and aspiring mechanics! 🚗⛽[/h2]

Today, we’re diving into a feature every dealership needs to master: refueling. Whether prepping a car for sale or making sure your latest acquisition runs smoothly, you’ll be spending some time at the pump. Let's take a closer look at how the refueling mechanic works in the Car Dealer Simulator and why it’s more than just topping off the tank!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/f7ec2c17e2ac7ffe231fd78e232859c6f63afb94.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Parking and Positioning: Fuel Up Like a Pro[/b][/h3]
First things first, when you roll up to the pump, it’s essential to get your car in the right spot. You’ll notice a visible zone next to the pump where your vehicle needs to be parked. Once you’re in position, the fun begins! With a click, you’ll grab the refueling gun, place it into the fuel filler, and get ready to refuel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/bd0f0a3712b877c3734dbc7818a70e607b0318cf.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Fueling Options: Manual or Automatic – The Choice is Yours[/b][/h3]
Once the gun is in place, the refueling UI pops up, and you’ve got two options. You can either manually fill the tank by holding the LMB or switch on the Auto Fill feature to make things easier. Auto Fill lets you fill the tank without holding the button, allowing the fuel to flow until the tank is full—or your wallet runs dry!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/2db2b36a692c6b30012d20a07edbb0431461b3a3.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Fuel Limits: Keep an Eye on the Gauge[/b][/h3]
The refueling interface is sleek and straightforward. As you pump gas, the numbers on the UI steadily increase, showing how much fuel you’re adding and how much it’ll cost. Whether you prefer to measure in liters or gallons, we’ve got you covered with units displayed in both formats. You can refuel as much as you need—up to a 60L tank capacity for the biggest cars or as much as your balance allows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44018181/f7db1b4713e3acf0f9cbf26f1b72953da75c8c37.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Transactions Made Simple[/b][/h3]
Once you’re done refueling, hit the button at the bottom of the UI to confirm your purchase. The game will notify you of the fuel added and the funds deducted from your account, so you’ll always know exactly where you stand. If you change your mind or realize you’re running low on cash, you can cancel the process and exit the UI anytime.

[h3][b]Seamless and Satisfying[/b][/h3]
The refueling mechanic is designed to feel as natural and smooth as possible, whether you prefer doing things manually or letting the Auto Fill handle it for you. Every refueling session becomes essential to maintaining your cars, getting them ready for the road, or primed for sale.

We’re looking forward to seeing how you handle your fleet’s fuel management. Stay tuned for more updates, and keep your tanks full!

— The Dev Team ⛽🚗

notes.title: A Closer Look at the Car Dealer Simulator’s Driving Mechanics
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/c2911e7c8126e2f98ace45b81e1f3ac6754e95c2.png[/img]

[h3]Hello Dealers,[/h3]

We’re excited to share an update on Car Dealer Simulator as we continue to improve the game ahead of its release. Today, we want to talk about something you’ve often asked about—our car-driving mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/88148bb99d88b8e1030b77b4eb0b6a66c0be7021.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Driving Mechanics Overview[/b][/h3]

As a car dealer, you won’t just be managing your dealership; you’ll also get behind the wheel to test-drive the cars yourself. To make sure this aspect of the game feels right, we’ve integrated the Chaos Vehicles System from Unreal Engine 5. This system brings a solid and responsive driving experience, ensuring that every car you test-drive feels distinct.

[h3][b]Key Features[/b][/h3]

Here are some of the highlights of what we’ve been working on:

[b]Physics-Based Driving:[/b] The Chaos Vehicles System allows for more realistic vehicle physics. While it’s not a hardcore simulation, you’ll notice the weight and handling of each car as you drive. It’s balanced to be accessible and authentic, giving you a good sense of how each vehicle performs.

[b]Responsive Handling: [/b]We’ve worked hard to make the driving controls responsive and intuitive. The handling should feel natural and satisfying, whether you’re taking a leisurely drive or pushing a car to see what it can do.

[b]Different Experience for Different Cars: [/b]Many of you wanted to know if there will be multiple car models and types. Of course! More than that, we are doing our best to make the driving experience of each car model a bit different. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138655/5028d3f83002a9860a70275cd9a2049a666fd580.gif[/img]

[h3][b]What’s yet to be done?[/b][/h3]

Here are some of the things from our current TODO list:

[b]Visual and Feedback Improvements: [/b]Our HUD is not final yet, so we are working on developing the right one – simple yet useful.
